beats.label: S1 · The Canterbury dies
beats.text: Holden's ice-hauler crew answers a distress call from the derelict Scopuli, only for a stealth ship to nuke their mothership and leave them as the sole witnesses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the inciting incident that turns Holden's civilians into the crew of the show and sets the conspiracy investigation in motion.

beats.label: S1 · Miller and Julie Mao
beats.text: On Ceres, Detective Miller is hired to find missing heiress Julie Mao and finds her tied to the same Scopuli distress call that just cost Holden his ship.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Julie's disappearance is the second, secretly-connected thread; without it the conspiracy would never surface.

beats.label: S1 · Avasarala smells a third player
beats.text: In New York, Avasarala baits the Martian ambassador with stolen stealth-tech intel and, from his panicked denial, realises a third player is trying to trigger an Earth-Mars war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes that the conspiracy is not Mars or Earth, and that Avasarala is the only politician actually looking for it.

beats.label: S1 · Donnager falls, Rocinante born
beats.text: Stealth ships destroy the Martian flagship Donnager; Holden's crew escapes on a Martian gunship they rename the Rocinante and take shelter with OPA-tied Fred Johnson at Tycho.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The ship and the crew's political alignment for the rest of the show are both forged here.

beats.label: S1 · Anubis is empty
beats.text: The crew boards the derelict stealth ship Anubis and finds no bodies, only a glowing substance fused to the reactor; they trace its shuttle to Eros hunting for Julie Mao.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First encounter with the protomolecule and the pivot from murder mystery to alien threat.

beats.label: S1 · Eros, the incubator
beats.text: Miller and Holden find Julie dead in a hotel bathroom, coated in the same substance; the entire Eros slum is being sealed in as an infection experiment by unseen conspirators.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the true scale and purpose of the conspiracy — a live weapons test on a whole station of people.

beats.label: S1 · Errinwright unmasked
beats.text: Miller and Holden barely escape Eros with lethal radiation doses; Avasarala works out that her own superior Errinwright is helping run the conspiracy from inside the UN itself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the political villain and the horror the next season inherits — Eros is loose, and Earth's government is compromised.

cliffhanger.text: Eros is quarantined but alive, an entire station rewritten by an alien substance no one on Earth or Mars actually controls. Avasarala knows the UN itself is compromised, and Holden's ragged crew are the only outsiders who have seen what happened there.
questions: What is the protomolecule doing to the people trapped on Eros?
Who is Jules-Pierre Mao really working for, and how deep does Errinwright's faction reach?
Can Holden's crew stay ahead of both Earth and Mars now that they carry the only evidence?

characters.name: James Holden
characters.line: Idealist ex-officer thrown into command of the salvaged Rocinante, now the reluctant face of the Canterbury attack after his broadcast blamed Mars.

characters.name: Naomi Nagata
characters.line: The Rocinante's Belter engineer, a quietly principled fixer who is becoming Holden's closest partner on the ship.

characters.name: Amos Burton
characters.line: Baltimore-born mechanic whose loyalty runs through Naomi and whose default answer to problems is violence.

characters.name: Alex Kamal
characters.line: Ex-Martian navy pilot flying the Rocinante, the crew's steady hand in the cockpit.

characters.name: Joe Miller
characters.line: Disgraced Ceres cop obsessed with Julie Mao, now travelling with Holden after nearly dying on Eros.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: UN deputy undersecretary running her own quiet war against the conspirators, now certain her own boss is one of them.

characters.name: Fred Johnson
characters.line: Tycho Station manager and secret OPA power broker, the crew's fragile ally after the Donnager.

characters.name: Jules-Pierre Mao
characters.line: Billionaire industrialist secretly funding the protomolecule; ordered the Eros experiment to continue even after his own daughter Julie died in it.

characters.name: Sadavir Errinwright
characters.line: Avasarala's UN superior, now revealed as Mao's inside man in Earth's government.

beats.label: S2 · Bobbie and the road to war
beats.text: Martian marine Bobbie Draper deploys to Phoebe only to see it nuked; Earth retaliates by destroying Mars's moon Deimos and both sides start marching toward open war.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Bobbie and establishes the Earth-Mars conflict that the protomolecule story rides on top of all season.

beats.label: S2 · Miller executes Dresden
beats.text: Fred Johnson leads a Belter strike on the Protogen research base at Thoth; before its lead scientist Dresden can talk his captors into continuing the project, Miller shoots him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Miller's decision to kill Dresden fractures his relationship with the crew and defines who he is in his last arc.

beats.label: S2 · Eros redirected, Miller dies
beats.text: To stop infected Eros reaching Earth, Miller stays behind with a nuke and coaxes the transformed Julie Mao inside to steer the whole asteroid into Venus instead, dying with it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Eros storyline, plants the protomolecule on Venus, and removes the show's original protagonist.

beats.label: S2 · Ganymede and the hybrid
beats.text: On the breadbasket moon Ganymede, Bobbie's squad is slaughtered by an inhuman figure; the resulting panic triggers an orbital battle that shatters the mirrors and starves the Belt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reveals the protomolecule has been weaponised into hybrids and creates the humanitarian crisis that drives the back half of the season.

beats.label: S2 · Prax joins the hunt
beats.text: The Rocinante takes in Ganymede botanist Prax, whose daughter Mei was taken by a Protogen doctor the hour the battle began; the trail leads to a new round of experiments on Belter children.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Anchors the mission that carries the crew to Io and gives the abstract weapons programme a human face.

beats.label: S2 · Bobbie defects, Mao cornered
beats.text: Bobbie escapes the Martian embassy on Earth with what she saw on Ganymede and hands it to Avasarala, who uses it to blackmail Jules-Pierre Mao out of hiding for a meeting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Locks Bobbie into Avasarala's camp and sets the ambush that closes the season.

beats.label: S2 · Naomi's sample, Venus stirs
beats.text: Mao's meeting turns into a firefight and he is captured; on Venus the Eros debris starts building something huge, and Naomi confesses she gave a protomolecule sample to Fred Johnson.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Three unresolved threads at once: Mao in Avasarala's hands, Venus active, Belters now holding a sample of the weapon.

cliffhanger.text: Mao is a prisoner but the protomolecule is loose everywhere at once — on Venus, on Tycho with Fred Johnson, and inside living Belter children being kept in stasis on Io. Everyone has a piece and nobody has control.
questions: What is the protomolecule building on Venus?
How many other children are being turned into hybrids, and who else is running the programme now that Mao is caught?
With Belters, Earth, and Mars all holding samples, who will use one first?

characters.name: James Holden
characters.line: Rocinante captain, sliding into vigilantism as he chases the protomolecule wherever it leads.

characters.name: Naomi Nagata
characters.line: Engineer and Holden's partner, quietly certain that the Belt needs its own protomolecule sample and willing to lie to her crew about it.

characters.name: Amos Burton
characters.line: The crew's enforcer, whose escalating brutality is starting to worry Holden.

characters.name: Alex Kamal
characters.line: Pilot holding the Rocinante together as the crew fractures around him.

characters.name: Bobbie Draper
characters.line: Martian marine turned defector, the only witness willing to describe the Ganymede hybrid.

characters.name: Praxideke Meng
characters.line: Ganymede botanist searching for his abducted daughter Mei, now travelling with the crew.

characters.name: Joe Miller
characters.line: Killed redirecting Eros into Venus, taking Julie Mao with him.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: UN operator who has forced Mao into her custody, but is still working alongside the very colleague who set the conspiracy in motion.

characters.name: Fred Johnson
characters.line: Tycho chief who now secretly holds the Belt's only protomolecule sample thanks to Naomi.

characters.name: Jules-Pierre Mao
characters.line: Protomolecule financier, now Avasarala's prisoner on Earth.

characters.name: Sadavir Errinwright
characters.line: UN undersecretary still moving openly beside Avasarala while running his own war and quietly poisoning Mars's defence minister.

beats.label: S3 · Frame-up in orbit
beats.text: Errinwright frames Avasarala for the Eros incident and orders her killed on Mao's yacht; she and Bobbie shoot their way to Mao's racing ship and are picked up in deep space by the Rocinante.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Avasarala and Bobbie onto the Rocinante for the rest of the season and hands Holden the leverage that will end Errinwright.

beats.label: S3 · Hybrid missiles neutralised
beats.text: Mao's scientists on Io load infected Ganymede children into hybrid missiles bound for Earth; the crew captures Mao's operation and Fred Johnson destroys the missiles in flight with stolen nukes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Mei/protomolecule-weapons plotline running since Ganymede and hands the OPA a decisive moment on the galactic stage.

beats.label: S3 · Errinwright falls
beats.text: Preacher Anna Volovodov, now advising the UN Secretary-General, uses a smuggled recording of Errinwright's confession to force his arrest and stop the Earth-Mars war mid-escalation.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the season's political villain and averts the war, freeing everyone to look at what Venus is doing.

beats.label: S3 · The Ring appears
beats.text: The Venus structure lifts off and reassembles beyond Uranus as an enormous alien Ring; Earth, Mars, and the newly recognised OPA each send fleets to investigate what it wants.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Pivots the whole series from a solar-system war to an alien-first-contact story and sets up every faction's stake in the Ring.

beats.label: S3 · Miller returns as Investigator
beats.text: Alone in his cabin, Holden starts seeing Miller — an 'Investigator' spun up by the protomolecule that steers him into the Ring and toward the alien station at its heart.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Miller-as-construct becomes the show's channel to the aliens and drives every choice Holden makes from here on.

beats.label: S3 · Clarissa's revenge
beats.text: On the UN flagship, tech Melba Koh unmasks as Mao's other daughter Clarissa; she frames Holden for a bombing and stows away aboard the OPA warship Behemoth to kill him herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Clarissa Mao, whose life-debt to Holden's crew becomes a recurring thread in later seasons.

beats.label: S3 · 1300 doors open
beats.text: The Ring station slams every ship to near-standstill; Anna and Holden's crew persuade the fleets to power down, and the station opens gates to 1300 new worlds before letting anyone leave.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the season by handing humanity a whole galaxy of colonies overnight, which is the setup the next season has to live with.

cliffhanger.text: An alien network to 1300 habitable systems has just switched on, and the Rocinante is the first ship through the gate. The Earth-Mars-Belt war is on hold and no political body owns what happens next.
questions: What is on the other side of those 1300 gates?
Now that Earth, Mars, and the Belt each hold Ring access, who decides who colonises what?
With Miller apparently gone, does the protomolecule still have a hand on Holden?

characters.name: James Holden
characters.line: Rocinante captain and the only human the alien Investigator speaks to.

characters.name: Naomi Nagata
characters.line: Engineer whose protomolecule secret cost her Holden's trust and slowly rebuilt it.

characters.name: Amos Burton
characters.line: The crew's enforcer, noticeably steadier around Holden after last season.

characters.name: Alex Kamal
characters.line: Pilot, quietly reconciled with his old Martian service through Bobbie.

characters.name: Bobbie Draper
characters.line: Ex-MCRN marine, now fully attached to Avasarala's inner circle.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: De facto UN power broker after Errinwright's public arrest.

characters.name: Camina Drummer
characters.line: Fred Johnson's second, captaining the OPA warship Behemoth after being crippled and given mechanical legs.

characters.name: Klaes Ashford
characters.line: Anderson Dawes's man, Drummer's first officer and the OPA voice for destroying the Ring at any cost.

characters.name: Anna Volovodov
characters.line: Methodist pastor turned political conscience of the UN, key to averting the war and standing down the fleets.

characters.name: Clarissa Mao
characters.line: Jules-Pierre's other daughter, jailed at season's end for trying to murder Holden.

characters.name: Joe Miller
characters.line: The dead detective, briefly present as a protomolecule Investigator inside Holden's head until the Ring station absorbed him.

beats.label: S4 · Rush to the new worlds
beats.text: Belter refugees defy Avasarala's blockade to settle the alien world Ilus; she sends Holden and his crew to broker peace between them and a Martian corporate expedition also landing there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the season's arena and the political tension that Marco will exploit — the Ring worlds are already a fight over who gets them.

beats.label: S4 · Miller reactivates Ilus
beats.text: Guided by a flickering Miller in his head, Holden pulls a root from an alien structure on Ilus and reactivates dormant protomolecule tech across the planet, calling down disasters.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the human colonisation problem into an alien-defence problem and re-opens the Miller channel.

beats.label: S4 · Murtry's private war
beats.text: RCE security chief Adolphus Murtry blames the Belters for a shuttle downing and starts executing them, while Ilus itself begins killing everyone with quakes, blindness and neurotoxic slugs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's ground-level conflict — a corporate strongman versus refugees — that the crew has to survive to reach the artifact.

beats.label: S4 · Bobbie on the wrong side of Mars
beats.text: On a decaying Mars, discharged Bobbie takes work with a criminal ring trafficking military hardware and realises most of the stolen gear is flowing to a single Belter buyer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the Mars-Belt weapons pipeline that will explain how Marco's fleet is armed.

beats.label: S4 · The Ilus shutdown
beats.text: Miller's construct builds itself a metal body, walks into the artifact at Ilus's core and shuts down every piece of protomolecule tech on the planet for good; he does not return.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Ilus threat and closes the Miller storyline that has driven Holden since the Ring opened.

beats.label: S4 · Ashford dies chasing Marco
beats.text: OPA peacekeeper Ashford tracks a Belter warlord named Marco Inaros — Naomi's estranged former lover — onto his ship, where Marco's son Filip ambushes Ashford so Marco can execute him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Marco and Filip properly, ties them to Naomi, and removes the one person who was already hunting them.

beats.label: S4 · Rocks toward Earth
beats.text: Avasarala loses re-election to pro-expansion Nancy Gao and is packed off to Luna; unnoticed by anyone, Marco Inaros launches a swarm of asteroids cloaked in Martian stealth tech at Earth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The literal setup of the next season — the attack is already in flight and the one politician who might have stopped it has just been fired.

cliffhanger.text: The protomolecule fight on Ilus is over, but a Belter warlord no one is watching has bought Martian stealth on the black market and thrown asteroids at Earth. The one person who saw it coming has just been ejected from power.
questions: Will Earth spot the incoming asteroids in time to stop them?
What does Marco Inaros actually want, and who else on Mars is arming him?
Now that Naomi knows her old lover has raised her son into a Belter zealot, will she try to reach Filip?

characters.name: James Holden
characters.line: Rocinante captain, at last free of Miller and the protomolecule voice in his head.

characters.name: Naomi Nagata
characters.line: Engineer confronted on Ilus with the high gravity her Belter body cannot handle, and freshly aware her son is Marco Inaros's enforcer.

characters.name: Amos Burton
characters.line: Rocinante enforcer who came apart on Ilus when brute force could not fix the situation.

characters.name: Alex Kamal
characters.line: Pilot who flew the Rocinante above Ilus while the ground crew nearly starved.

characters.name: Bobbie Draper
characters.line: Ex-MCRN, tangled with a Mars weapons-trafficking gang after failing to make an honest life on a broken planet.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: Deposed UN Secretary-General, in exile on Luna as the crisis she predicted begins.

characters.name: Camina Drummer
characters.line: OPA captain of Medina Station in the Ring space, Ashford's ally in trying to police the Belt from within.

characters.name: Klaes Ashford
characters.line: OPA peacekeeper, killed by Marco Inaros while trying to bring him in.

characters.name: Marco Inaros
characters.line: Belter warlord, Naomi's former lover and Filip's father; has just launched a stealth asteroid attack on Earth.

characters.name: Filip Inaros
characters.line: Marco's teenage son and enforcer, and Naomi's biological son, raised entirely without her.

beats.label: S5 · Crew scatters
beats.text: With the Rocinante docked at Tycho, the crew scatters — Amos to Earth for a funeral, Alex home to Mars, Bobbie chasing traffickers, Naomi off alone to find her son Filip on Pallas.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splitting the crew across the system is what allows Marco's attack to catch everyone in a different fight.

beats.label: S5 · The rocks land
beats.text: Marco Inaros's stealth asteroids slam into Earth, killing millions and paralysing its government; he broadcasts himself as leader of a Free Navy and rightful ruler of the Belt and the Ring gates.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event the whole show has been building toward — Earth is broken and there is a new political power in the Belt.

beats.label: S5 · Fred Johnson dies
beats.text: A saboteur inside Tycho assassinates Fred Johnson, hands the Free Navy the last known protomolecule sample, and rigs the Rocinante to blow at launch; Naomi's warning to Holden saves the ship.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the OPA's steadying hand, hands the season's weapon to Marco, and confirms his reach inside every faction.

beats.label: S5 · Naomi on the Pella
beats.text: Aboard Marco's ship, Naomi cannot turn Filip against his father and instead uncovers Marco's plan to bait and destroy the Rocinante using Filip's own ship, the Chetzemoka.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Naomi at the centre of the season's climax and forces her to choose the crew over her son a second time.

beats.label: S5 · Amos and Clarissa on Earth
beats.text: Trapped in a maximum-security prison during the strikes, Amos breaks out with inmate Clarissa Mao and fights his way across a shattered Earth to a stolen shuttle bound for Luna.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rehabilitates Clarissa into the crew's orbit and gives the show its ground-level view of what the attack actually did.

beats.label: S5 · The trap, and Alex
beats.text: Naomi jumps ship in a suit toward the rigged Chetzemoka and distorts its fake distress call enough to warn Holden; Bobbie plucks her out just as Alex dies of a stroke pulling the manoeuvre.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rescues Naomi at the cost of Alex, leaving the crew reunited but permanently short a member.

beats.label: S5 · Free Navy takes the Ring
beats.text: The crew regroups on Luna under a restored Secretary-General Avasarala; meanwhile Marco's fleet, aided by rogue Martian warships, seizes the Ring space and the road to every colony world.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the strategic situation the finale opens on — Marco has already won the piece of the map that matters most.

cliffhanger.text: Earth is broken, Alex is dead, Mars is fracturing, and Marco Inaros holds the gate to 1300 worlds. Avasarala is back in charge with the Rocinante as her cudgel, but the Free Navy has already taken the piece of the board that matters most.
questions: How does the Inner alliance dislodge Marco from the Ring without a real fleet?
Where does Filip go now that Naomi has walked away from him a second time?
What is on the other side of the Ring that Marco has traded so much to control?

characters.name: James Holden
characters.line: Rocinante captain, reunited with what is left of his crew on Luna under Avasarala's flag.

characters.name: Naomi Nagata
characters.line: Engineer, out of Marco's custody, hollowed out by having failed to reach Filip.

characters.name: Amos Burton
characters.line: Rocinante enforcer, back with the crew and vouching for Clarissa Mao as his new charge.

characters.name: Bobbie Draper
characters.line: Ex-marine, formally joining Avasarala's staff after pulling Naomi out of vacuum.

characters.name: Clarissa Mao
characters.line: Amos's charge, brought under the Rocinante's protection at Holden's grudging consent.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: Restored UN Secretary-General after leading a cabinet revolt over the Pallas strike.

characters.name: Camina Drummer
characters.line: Belter running her own crew-family, coerced into alliance with Marco but visibly disgusted by him.

characters.name: Marco Inaros
characters.line: Free Navy leader, holder of the last protomolecule sample and effective ruler of the Ring gate.

characters.name: Filip Inaros
characters.line: Marco's son, publicly named heir and publicly humiliated after his uncle Cyn died helping Naomi escape.

characters.name: Alex Kamal
characters.line: Killed by an acceleration stroke pulling the manoeuvre that saved Naomi.

beats.label: S6 · Laconia beyond the Rings
beats.text: On the alien world Laconia beyond the Rings, a girl named Cara plays with living 'strange dogs' while Admiral Duarte's scientists coax an orbital protomolecule structure back to life.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the hidden third power the whole finale rides on — an off-screen faction with alien tech Earth and Mars know nothing about.

beats.label: S6 · Ceres empty
beats.text: Earth and Mars retake Ceres unopposed and find it stripped bare; Marco has abandoned the station, and his agents detonate a bomb in the docks as the Joint Fleet moves in to feed the refugees.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows Marco choosing to lose Ceres deliberately and forces the Inners into a costly humanitarian occupation.

beats.label: S6 · Drummer joins Avasarala
beats.text: Drummer's clan raids Free Navy depots and publicly calls Marco a coward; Naomi persuades her old friend to meet Avasarala, and Drummer's Belters formally join the Inner alliance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Splits the Belt for the first time — Marco is no longer the sole Belter voice, and the war becomes winnable.

beats.label: S6 · Holden spares Filip
beats.text: Bobbie ambushes Marco's ship the Pella and has him dead in the water; Holden disarms the killing torpedo when he sees Filip on the screen, letting Marco escape and splitting his own crew.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The choice that keeps the war alive into the finale and puts Holden's crew at odds with each other for the rest of the season.

beats.label: S6 · Laconian guns on the Ring
beats.text: A Martian strike force is annihilated by heavy railguns Marco has emplaced on the Ring station itself, exposing that the Free Navy has been armed all along by a Laconian faction beyond the Rings.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Connects the Marco war and the Laconia thread into one problem and shows how badly the Inners are outgunned.

beats.label: S6 · Marco eaten in the gate
beats.text: Disillusioned Filip abandons the Pella on a skiff before the final battle; the crew wakes the Ring entities as Marco's fleet transits, and they consume him and the Free Navy alive inside the gate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the Marco war and puts the alien entities on the map as the next existential problem, all in one moment.

beats.label: S6 · Transport Union
beats.text: Earth, Mars, and Drummer's Belt form an independent Transport Union to govern the Rings; Holden accepts its presidency, hands it straight to Drummer, and the Rocinante flies on into open space.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The settlement everyone has been fighting for — Belter sovereignty and a shared authority over the gates — and the crew's final position within it.

cliffhanger.text: Marco is dead and the Belt has its independence, but the Ring gates still lead to a Laconian empire the Inner powers have never met. Filip is loose somewhere in the Belt, the entities that ate Marco are still eating passing ships, and the Rocinante has traded a war for a much larger unanswered question.
questions: Who is Admiral Duarte, and what does his Laconian faction want with the protomolecule?
What are the entities on the other side of the gates, and what did they do to the Ring Builders?
With the Belt sovereign and Filip in the wind, is Naomi's story with her son actually over?

characters.name: Naomi Nagata

characters.name: Clarissa Mao

characters.name: Bobbie Draper
characters.line: Ex-marine turned the Rocinante's tactical hand, the one who almost ended the war a season early.

characters.name: Camina Drummer
characters.line: Belter faction leader turned inaugural president of the Transport Union.

characters.name: Chrisjen Avasarala
characters.line: UN Secretary-General, architect of the alliance that broke Marco.

characters.name: Marco Inaros
characters.line: Free Navy leader, consumed by the Ring entities along with his fleet.

characters.name: Filip Inaros
characters.line: Naomi's son, alive somewhere in the Belt after quietly abandoning his father before the final battle.

characters.name: Winston Duarte
characters.line: Leader of the hidden Laconian settlement beyond the Rings, and the source of the Free Navy's heavy weapons.
characters.note: Named admiral in source; role expanded but position stated in the summaries.

characters.name: Cara
characters.line: Laconian child whose younger brother Xan has been 'fixed' by the strange protomolecule dogs after his death.
